meta.title: SSD1306 OLED driver: framebuffer, font and refresh rate
meta.tools: C firmware (framebuffer + 5×7 font + line drawing), simulated SSD1306 page memory, Python image render
meta.summary: Render text, a line and a sine plot into a 128×64 monochrome framebuffer using the SSD1306 page layout, 'send' it over a simulated 400 kHz I²C link, rebuild the panel image from the transferred bytes and compute the achievable frame rate.
meta.problem: Small OLEDs store pixels in vertical 8-pixel 'pages'. Build a driver that gets the bit ordering right, and work out how fast the screen can actually be updated.
meta.theory:
128×64 pixels = 1,024 bytes (8 pages × 128 columns, bit 0 = top pixel of each page). Over I²C each byte costs 9 clocks: at 400 kHz a full
frame is ≥ 1,024×9/400 k ≈ 23 ms → ≈ 43 frames/s maximum (plus addressing overhead).
meta.method:
Firmware draws into uint8_t fb[1024] using the SSD1306 layout, then streams it with the 0x40 data prefix; the simulated panel writes
received bytes into its own GDDRAM in horizontal addressing mode and dumps it; Python renders the panel memory.

rows.quantity: Bytes per frame on the bus (1,024 data + 32 prefixes + 7 cmd)
